rationale: Tentative: in the immediate context of chirotonia (χειροτονία 'laying-on of hands') and a sequence of greeting-gestures (peace / X / blessing / joy), ⲭⲓⲛ may be a Coptic adaptation of Greek χείρ 'hand,' or possibly a Lycopolitan form related to ϫⲓⲝ 'hand.' Confidence low.

Tentative: appears as fourth member of greeting series 'peace / hand / blessing / X.' Possibly Lycopolitan reflex of ⲣⲣⲉ-/ⲃⲣ̄ⲣⲉ root or a noun of exultation. Could also relate to ⲡⲣⲏ 'sun/radiance.' Lexical identification uncertain.

Lycopolitan orthographic variant of ⲡⲥⲏⲩ 'the time' (parallel to ⲡⲥⲁⲡ used elsewhere on the page). The ⲥⲭⲩ spelling is unusual; sense fixed by the formulaic phrase ⲙ̄ⲡⲥⲭⲩ ⲉⲧϥⲛⲏⲩ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'at the time when he comes forth.'
Compound verb of sending: ⲧⲡⲟ/ⲑⲡⲟ stem 'cause to go' + ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'forth.' Used here of the cosmic farewell — the gods escort the First Man forth to combat while embracing him.

Restored by the editor with [ⲁⲡϣ]; the visible ⲭϩ does not correspond to any standard Coptic root I can identify. Context (parallel to ⲡⲁⲅⲱⲛ 'contest' in surrounding lines, modified by 'of the lower side') suggests a synonym for the cosmic combat / descent. Lexical identification pending.
